angle: Movement translation, DL (clearest of five groups screened, Fig 2C): each lineman's tracked Combine 40 start laid over his own random NFL pass-rush starts (combine_frames vs game_frames_sample). The curve does not translate after size (rho 0.07 [-0.14, 0.28], n=67; ceiling with two reps 0.67; P(true >= 0.5) = 0.03; no per-player similarity score above 0.18 vs pressure beyond pick). Agreement between the official 40 time and the NFL first step does explain pressure beyond pick, tested as a held-out 'Both' shortlist used to hand out passing-down snaps.
metric_name: Speed that translates ('Both'): NFL first step (speed 0.3-0.5 s after first movement on ~20 random sampled pass rushes, alignment-adjusted, in sd after weight and EDGE share) in the top third AND official 40 time in the top half; cut-offs for each class set on the other two classes
headline_number: Pool = 69 of 118 DL (33 with <8 sampled starts, 16 with <100 rushes excluded). Both shortlist beats the held-out pick/weight/role pressure forecast 8 of 10 vs 16 of 59 (gap 53 pts [28, 75], shuffle p 0.009); IPW for reaching the pool 53 [27, 77]; frozen after 2024 and scored on 2025 vs persistence 6 of 7 vs 6 of 16; day-3 only 2 of 3 vs 9 of 33 (unproven). Continuous: NFL first step +0.8 pressure-rate pts per sd [0.1, 1.4] held out; rusher random-intercept model 0.7 [0.2, 1.2].
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_14/cand_3 (7.90), applying the round-14 judges' top_changes by analogy. Writeup: short title; three-sentence lede (~55 words) with one count; 'Why it matters' rewritten around the post-rookie snap/veteran decision; one-sentence metric; one bold verdict paragraph that collapses the hedges (real but modest in the full pool, unproven for day 3); analyst detail moved to the appendix; the 6-row board table replaced by a worked decision case. Football: worked decision case on a real board (Cedric Johnson vs Javontae Jean-Baptiste, 2024 day-3 edges 8 picks apart, both $1.04M rookie APY; call frozen from 2024 data only; 2025 outcome; rule edge 6.4 pressures/season vs a $5.5M median for 2025's 21st-40th veteran edge contracts, OTC via nflverse); measurement protocol (24+ random rushes for reliability 0.7; no extra Combine 40 reps since 90% of DL already run two); 40 clip-start issue addressed (curves anchored at first movement); 2026 list now carries alignment (hand-down end / interior) and games missed. Corrected a round-14 error: WR NFL starts are readable (reliability 0.72) but do not pay; only OL/DB/TE are too noisy. Data science: exclusions reported; selection model P(pool) from pick, weight, 40, class (AUC 0.85) with first step not predicting selection (OR 0.81, p 0.52); stabilized IPW reruns of slope and shortlist gap; rusher random-intercept binomial GLMM (Gauss-Hermite) on 137 player-seasons; shuffle p moved into Table 2; shortlist calibration from the other two classes (expected 69% vs observed 80%; Brier 0.212 vs 0.253). Viz: Fig 2 gains panel C (five-group screen; groups with reliability < 0.3 greyed, DL row uses the text's numbers); Fig 3 title now states what the data support (edge narrows, unproven for day 3), p labels match Table 2, label collisions fixed.
open_risks: The two-signal form was chosen in round 12 after seeing all three classes; only the cut-offs are held out. The 2026 class is the first blind test (slope test power 47%)
Day-3 evidence is thin: 3 shortlisted day-3 rushers (2 of 3 hit, shuffle p 0.22); the time-forward continuous slope beyond persistence is +0.4 [-0.5, 1.3]

Worked decision case is post hoc in choice of pair; Jean-Baptiste played 3 games in 2025, so the outcome cannot score the call; the dollar comparison (rookie APY vs veteran-tier APY) is football context, not a valuation model of pressures
Games missed counts games without a recorded snap (injury, inactive or cut), not injury reports
